assessments.reasoning: Eclipse's 1.0 section 3 opening and conditions at [3552,4573) identify the distribution form, whose agreement must carry the statement, who supplies the source, and what recipients must be told. The following source-form conditions do not impose physical source bundling on the object-code route.

challenge.method: Compared an agreement identifying the distributing Contributor's source offering and giving usable retrieval directions with an unrelated upstream pointer alone and with a statement of availability omitting retrieval directions. Then compared the subsequent source-form paragraph.
challenge.results: The first agreement supplies both required elements. The unrelated pointer alone fails to identify source available from the distributing Contributor. An availability statement without directions fails the second element. Reasonable access can be provided separately from the object code. The source-form paragraph instead requires EPL availability and an agreement copy with each source copy.

limitations: Section 3(a) and 3(b)(i)–(iii) impose additional conditions. Meeting (iv) alone does not establish compliance with section 3.
The adequacy of any actual source offering or access channel depends on what source is available and how licensees can obtain it.
reasoning: For the EPL 1.0 option of distributing object code under the Contributor's own agreement, section 3(b)(iv) requires two things in that agreement. It must identify that Contributor as the source of the Program's source code and tell licensees how to obtain it reasonably through a customary software-exchange medium.
